title: Terp Standard finding
description: The machine-readable finding a conformant checker emits: an array of these objects per checked tree. The corpus contract is stated over this shape — for a rule under test, every violation-* case yields at least one finding whose `rule` is the catalog id, and every compliant-* case yields none for that rule. Findings are attributed to the stack-neutral catalog id, never a tool-internal rule id.

rule.description: The Terp Standard catalog id the finding realises (catalog/<surface>/<rule>.json).

path.description: File path relative to the checked tree's root (the corpus case root, or the app root), with forward slashes.

line.description: 1-based line of the violation, when the checker can locate it.

message.description: Human-readable explanation; ideally directive (states the compliant fix).

fix_hint.description: Agent-oriented remediation metadata: the compliant construct that replaces the violating one, sourced from the catalog entry's non-normative `reference` field (or the checker's own knowledge of the sanctioned pattern). Optional — a consumer must not require it.

fingerprint.description: A stable, checker-chosen identifier for THIS violation instance (e.g. a hash over rule + path + violating source construct), so consumers can track a finding across line-shifting edits. Optional; the fingerprint scheme is checker-internal — only stability across reformatting is expected.
